summary: The literal n=1 endpoint of Theorem 1.4 and its matrix lemma fails. The nontrivial n>=2 derivation and asymptotic rates are not refuted. No major or critical defect is established in the inspected scope.

problems.title: The logarithmic covariance bound needs a sample-size qualification
problems.claim_status: False at n=1 under the literal positive-integer reading; valid intended n>=2 interpretation considered

problems.evidence: For any unit v=(a,b), each sample gives projected squared W2 cost (|a|-|b|)^2/2. Its supremum is 1/2, attained at an axis; expectation is therefore 1/2. RHS at n=1 is zero. Independent exact rational transport check confirms 48 finite cases.
problems.check_result: Analytic universal counterexample proved; corroborating computation exit 0 and all assertions passed.
counterevidence: The proof choices ceil(log n) support an intended n>=2 reading. Under that restriction the counterexample is not admissible.
For n>=2 the matrix moment, symmetrization and dual-ball derivation were followed without a demonstrated substantive failure.
Corollary 2.9's conclusion survives n=1 by direct Gaussian comparison even though its displayed parameter choice does not.
The official current arXiv record lists v6; publisher complete theorem text was not accessed. No assertion is made that the journal version has the same wording.
problems.core_dependency: Lemma 3.2 -> equation (3.2) quadratic lift; Corollary 2.9 -> matrix empirical-process bound; Lemma 3.1 -> logarithmic n estimate in Theorem 1.4. At n=1 the positive Schatten moment selection fails and its asserted estimates can be false.
problems.impact: A supported local sample-size defect, not an invalidation of the nontrivial n>=2 or asymptotic contribution. Severity rests on the restricted endpoint damage, not merely on ease of repair or survival of the whole paper.

correction.statement: Either restrict the logarithmic matrix bound and Theorem 1.4 to n>=2, treating n=1 separately where needed; or replace log n by log(en) in the expanded bound for n>=1.
correction.verification: For n>=2 monotonicity log(en)>=log n uses the checked proof. For n=1 squared projected W2 <=4r^2 and log(e)=1, so universal C>=4 suffices. Kappa=0 implies mu=delta0 directly.

independent_verification.decisive_source_claim: Theorem 1.4, pp.6 and 22, states a bound on the expected squared max-sliced Wasserstein distance with ln(n), without an n>=2 restriction. Lemma 3.1, p.20, has the same endpoint defect.
independent_verification.hypotheses_checked: For n=1, the uniform law on {+e1,-e1,+e2,-e2} is symmetric, supported in the radius-one Euclidean ball, with covariance I_2/2 and strictly positive operator norm. Thus the stated hypotheses, including symmetry and bounded support, hold.
independent_verification.independent_derivation: For every sample and unit direction (a,b), the projected squared W2 cost is (|a|-|b|)^2/2. Symmetric one-dimensional transport equals transport of absolute radii: the absolute-value map gives the lower bound, while optimal radii coupled with a common symmetric sign attain it. The supremum is exactly 1/2, attained on a coordinate axis, so its expectation is 1/2. The printed upper bound is zero because ln(1)=0. For Lemma 3.1 the uniform law on the six signed coordinate vectors in R3 gives left side 1 and first right side 2/3 at n=1; the second Gaussian estimate also has positive left side and zero right side.
independent_verification.counterevidence_and_scope: The proof uses p=ceil(ln n), requiring p>=1. The n>=2 argument inspected on pp.20-23 uses valid rank, moment, and quadratic estimates. Programmatic convention search over all 27 pages, followed by reading the relevant notation and hits, found no global n>=2 or truncated-log convention. The defect is confined to the finite endpoint; it does not refute the intended asymptotic rates. Corollary 2.9 at n=1 can be bounded directly by 2 E||X|| and its Gaussian term, so it is not additionally alleged false.
independent_verification.repair_checked: Restrict the theorem and logarithmic lemma to n>=2, or use ln(en). For n=1 the support bound gives W2^2<=4r^2, which is absorbed by the repaired expression with an absolute constant at least 4. For n>=2 the logarithm only increases. Zero covariance means X=0 almost surely and is handled separately.
independent_verification.severity_reason: Minor because the demonstrated failure concerns the omitted finite-sample endpoint while the n>=2 estimates and central rates remain intact; no broader theorem failure is claimed.
independent_verification.reused_calculation_facts: Fully read checks/boundary_n1.stdout.json and checks/execution.json. The 48 exact rational sample/direction costs agree with the independently derived formula; the historic Python execution is attributed to its original timestamp, not rerun or relabeled as current. The analytic all-direction proof, not the finite grid, establishes the supremum.
independent_verification.report_disposition: No report correction required; exact-current English TeX/PDF and bounded version/coverage statements agree with the verified finding.
